title: Atomic‐Scale Insights Into the Thermal Stability of High‐Entropy Nanoalloys

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Equiatomic five‑metal high‑entropy nanoalloy catalysts, likely ~3–5 nm FCC nanoparticles of noble‑metal HEA composition (e.g., Pt–Pd–Rh–Ru–Ir) supported on carbon.
recollection.intervention: Guess: In‑situ aberration‑corrected STEM heating experiments (to ~700–800 °C) with atomic‑resolution ADF‑STEM plus STEM‑EDS/EELS spectrum imaging to map element distributions during annealing, complemented by DFT/cluster‑expansion Monte Carlo to extract segregation and mixing energetics and by coarsening‑kinetics analysis.
recollection.structure: Guess: Initially a single‑phase FCC random solid solution; with heating it develops a compositional gradient/core–shell character (Pt/Pd enriched shell; Ru/Ir/Rh enriched core) while retaining FCC crystallinity and remaining largely single‑phase at the nanoscale, with limited particle coarsening.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Thermal stability governed by competition between surface‑energy–driven segregation (lower‑surface‑energy elements migrate to the surface) and configurational entropy that favors mixing; coarsening controlled predominantly by surface‑diffusion–limited Ostwald ripening/coalescence; element‑specific ‘sluggish’ diffusion and emergent local chemical order at surfaces slow phase separation.
recollection.results: Guess: Onset of measurable surface segregation around 450–550 °C; surface enrichment of Pt/Pd by ~20–40 at% relative to the bulk after annealing; coarsening kinetics consistent with surface diffusion (growth exponent n≈4) and an effective activation energy ~1.6–1.9 eV; particle sizes grow modestly (e.g., ~4.2±0.8 nm to ~5.6±1.1 nm after 1 h at 700 °C in inert gas) compared with monometallic or binary controls that coarsen to ~10–12 nm; simulation‑derived segregation energies on the order of −0.2 to −0.5 eV for Pt/Pd to the surface and positive for Ru/Ir/Rh, with no bulk phase separation detected up to ~700–800 °C under inert conditions.

score.note: Correctly anticipated in situ high-temperature aberration-corrected STEM near the actual 973 K endpoint, but added incorrect simulation/analytical methods. The alloy composition, shell species, structural evolution, and claimed stability/coarsening were wrong. Surface-energy-driven segregation was identified, but the recollection incorrectly invoked sluggish diffusion and entropy-stabilized mixing, opposite to the paper’s kinetic, non-sluggish behavior. It missed the 22% size reduction and supplied unsupported quantitative values.
